The first thing to understand is your credit will be shot. You can kiss any hopes of large purchases goodbye, because no-one is going to lend you money for a very long time.

Bankruptcy isn't free. In exchange for bankruptcy protection, you have to sell off as much as you can toward your debt. Depending on how you file, you may be able to keep up to a certain dollar amount goods. You don't own a home (and after filing bankruptcy, you likely won't for some time), so equity isn't a concern for you, but if it were, you would only be able to keep $18,500 worth of equity. There are certain exempt commodities, such as a 401k, with no dollar limit.

Everything else will be sold off by court order to pay off your creditors. However, there are no rules preventing you from buying your property back - bankruptcy trustees don't care who buys what, as long as they get a fair value.
